jobs.occupation: Technical assistant (m/f/d) (16/2026) (Biologisch-technische/r Assistent/in)
jobs.description: Your area of responsibility Research topic: Plant immunity Plant pathogens secrete small molecules in their host to manipulate cellular processes and cause disease. Plants are not defenseless, however, and have evolved a wide variety of immune receptors to sense these pathogen-associated molecules and subsequently trigger an immune response to restrict pathogen infection. In the Molecular Plant Immunity research group, we investigate the molecular basis of effector recognition and immune receptor activation, and how evolutionary forces shape these processes. We then leverage this knowledge to develop strategies for sustainable disease resistance in crops. Your tasks:• Independent execution of molecular biology laboratory tasks• Microbiological work with bacteria and fungi under sterile conditions• Organization and maintenance of standardized workflows in the laboratory• Plant husbandry• Support lab members in their experiments• Documenting experimental procedures and resultsYour profile• Completed training as a Biological technical assistant or equivalent• Independent and solution-oriented work ethic• Enthusiasm for teamwork• Ability to work in a multi-cultural, multi-ethnic environment with sensitivity and respect for diversity• Desirable knowledge and skills include:• Good English language skills (written and spoken)• Experience in microbiology and molecular biology work• Experience in handling biosafety S1 organismsPlease apply with a cover letter and your CV containing the contact details of two referees and by the 7th of December 2026. If you have any questions, please contact Clemence Marchal (clemence.marchal@ipb-halle.de).We offer• Modern Working Conditions: Comprehensive introduction to work techniques and a modern research environment with state-of-the-art equipment and up-to-date software• Career Development: Targeted training opportunities and access to a specialized library with electronic resources and quiet workspaces• Compensation & Security: Classification according to TV-L including annual bonus, pension scheme (VBL), health offers, and discounted canteen meals• Ideal Working Environment: A varied and inspiring workplace in an international setting at a leading scientific and innovation hub• Team Spirit and Leadership Culture: An open culture that strengthens teamwork, enables career networking, and promotes your research skills.• Work-Life Balance: Flexible working models, remote work options, and 30 days of annual leave – for a balanced work-life experience.About us The Leibniz Institute of Plant Biochemistry (IPB) is a non-university research institution of the Leibniz Association on the Weinberg Campus of the Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg. As a foundation under public law, the IPB is under direct supervision of the state of Saxony-Anhalt.The IPB is an internationally recognized research institution and consists of four scientific Departments, additional independent junior research groups, and the Department Administration & Infrastructure (about 200 employees, including about 40 PhD students). Research at the IPB aims to understand the (bio)chemical basis of plant resilience and performance in challenging environments related to climate change. The IPB offers excellent research facilities and state-of-the-art infrastructure to investigate the chemical diversity, biochemical interactions, and biological roles of small natural molecules in plants and fungi, with an emphasis on specialized metabolites, chemical mediators, and relevant molecular networks of functional gene and protein regulation (https://www.ipb-halle.de/en/).Dr. Clemence MarchalResearch AssociateTelefon: 0345 55821440clemence.marchal@ipb-halle.deLeibniz-Institut für Pflanzenbiochemie (IPB)Weinberg 306120 Halle (Saale)

jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in geography – Assessing socio-economic impacts of climate extremes (Geograf/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Institute for Geography at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences seeks to fill the above position.The PhD position is part of the project “CASCADE – Cascading impacts of climate extremes: new perspectives for interlinking Earth System Sciences in Leipzig” on compound and cascading impacts of climate extremes. CASCADE investigates how floods and droughts affect society and the environment, combining large-scale data analysis with a systems perspective on human–environment interactions.Our knowledge of the impacts of climate extremes is only as good as the data that record them. The PhD project aims to uncover biases in climate impact databases and research and to provide a more comprehensive view of flood and drought impacts at the global scale. To this end, the doctoral researcher will link and harmonise existing databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, EM-DAT) into a common event, impact and spatial framework, and will contribute to developing a multilingual news-based impact dataset that helps to fill gaps in existing sources. Using independent global hazard and exposure data as a reference, the project will analyse where and for which impacts the sources agree, how reported magnitudes differ, and how the likelihood that an event is recorded at all depends on hazard severity, exposure, socioeconomic conditions, language and media presence.The project benefits from close collaboration with the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ). The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team at the interface of geography, climate-risk research and data science.About the position- Salary group 13  TV-L - Fixed term of 3 years, Qualification-related purposes - 75 % of a full-time position, part-time employment possible- Start date: 1 March 2027The role- Linking and harmonisation of text-based and established impact databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, news-based data, EM-DAT) into a common global event, impact and spatial framework- Comparative analysis of where, when and for which impact types the datasets converge or diverge, using global hazard and exposure data as an independent reference- Analysis of the geographical, socioeconomic and linguistic factors that shape the visibility of impacts in different data sources- Development of a combined, bias-aware global view of flood and drought impacts- Contribution to the development and validation of a multilingual news-based impact dataset using natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs)- Publication of results in international peer-reviewed journals, presentation at scientific conferences and open publication of code and dataAbout you- University degree (e.g. master’s) or equivalent in geography, computational social sciences, digital humanities, environmental or earth system sciences, disaster risk research or a closely related field- Experience in data analysis, in particular in combining and harmonising heterogeneous datasets, e.g. demonstrated through the master’s thesis, research projects or work experience- Excellent programming skills (e.g. Python, R)- Experience in the analysis of spatial data, e.g. spatial statistics- Interest in climate-risk, natural-hazard or disaster research, e.g. demonstrated through coursework or the master’s thesis- Very good written and spoken English (at least language proficiency level B2)- Experience with, or demonstrable interest in, natural language processing or large language models preferable, e.g. through coursework or projectsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application addressed to Prof. Dr. Miguel Mahecha, Institute’s Director, by 23 November 2026 via our online application portal (https://uni-leipzig.b-ite.careers/en/jobposting/68a780049a96ddf8d6fa4bea19873171c42d4e1f0/apply) .Your application should include:Cover letter; CV; copies of degree certificates and transcripts; a research statement (max. 2 pages) outlining how the applicant would approach combining impact datasets and identifying their biases and blind spots; summary or excerpt from your master’s thesis or another writing sample; contact details of two refereesIf you have any questions about the role, please contact Prof. Dr. Mariana Madruga de Brito, Professor, 0341 60252149.

jobs.description: About GFGlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors that enable AI at scale, from the cloud to the physical world. We partner closely with our customers to deliver differentiated, power-efficient, high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. Across our global footprint in the United States, Europe and Asia, our teams are solving complex challenges that shape the future of technology. At GF, you'll find the opportunity to make an impact, work with world-class talent and contribute to a more secure, sustainable future.Your JobIn semiconductor manufacturing, no processing machine runs continuously yielding the same results. Materials used in the machine can degrade over time, simple factors like –outside temperature can fluctuate, and high usage and low usage play a roll. For stable process results, specific machine settings and recipe parameters are tuned automatically or manually. This is an essential part of work for our process and equipment experts.As a PhD candidate, you will be looking differently at our machines and processes. You already have a scientist´s or an engineer´s view. You know and see the parameters available, regardless of current usage. There, your journey starts towards finding the optimal machine and process settings with as few as possible latest data points. Latest advances in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence indicate the possibility for improvements and will guide your research.The goal of this work shall be the summary and testing of state-of-the-art methods in real-world applications as well as development of new methods tailored to the needs of the semiconductor industry, so in this work Data Science approaches are to be developed to enable process experts to use ML and AI for machine and process tuning.   The contract for this position is set up for 3 years with the possibility to extend it by one additional year, if required. We are looking for a research associate who wants to take a coordinating role in a joint project with other partners from academia and industry and in aligning their research work to the requirements of later mass production. jobs.description: Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:Technische Informatik; Software-Engineering; Künstliche Intelligenz; InformationswissenschaftStellenbeschreibung:As part of the German government's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, the successful Saxon competence center ScaDS.AI Dresden/Leipzig (Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence) is being expanded into a leading German AI competence center for Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI). For TUD Dresden University of Technology, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At the Center for Interdisciplinary Digital Sciences (CIDS), the Department for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (ScaDS.AI Dresden) offers, subject to the availability of resources, two project positions funded by the BMFTR asResearch Associate / PostDoc (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting as soon as possible. The positions are fixed-term until March 31, 2029. The individual contract duration will be determined according to the candidate’s qualifications and the intended academic qualification goal. An extension may be possible subject to the availability of resources. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). A shorter contract term is possible by arrangement. Within the project Neuro-Symbolic AI with Logic-Memory Decomposition (Neuro-SAIL), a new class of architectures for verifiable neuro-symbolic AI is being researched using Logic-Memory Decomposition. Rule-based decisions are made by logic components, while memory modules are only used when information is incomplete or ambiguous. If no reliable decision is possible, escalation to humans occurs. The aim is to make rule-based decisions more transparent and efficient, to limit the use of neural models to necessary cases, and to reduce rule violations and unsubstantiated statements.Professional assignment: Chair of Scalable Software Architectures for Data Analytics (Prof. Dr. Michael Färber)Research areas: Natural Language Processing, Large Language Models, Knowledge Graphs, and related fields (e.g., Graph Machine Learning)Tasks: - scientific research and development activities in at least one of the above-mentioned research areas- participation in national and international research projects, possibly in collaboration with industry- preparation of publications in internationally renowned journals and presentation of research findings at conferencesRequirements: - a university degree (M.Sc., M.Eng. or equivalent) and if applicable a PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Systems, Data Science, Computational Science, Mathematics, Applied Statistics, Information Science, Information Systems, Information Systems Engineering, Electronic Information Engineering, Computational Linguistics, Digital Humanities, Linguistics, or a related field- a strong interest in fundamental research in the above-mentioned fields- strong programming skills, preferably in Python, including experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow) and related tools- good written and spoken English- strong analytical and problem-solving skills- high level of motivation and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team- research experience (publications, theses, projects) in the above-mentioned research areas is a major advantageWe offer:The position comes with access to high-performance computing resources and access to training opportunities within ScaDS.AI.TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for oneResearch associate (m/f/x) for the CRC 1844 "Episodic Memory", Subproject A16The Department of Predictive Cognition is a newly established research unit within the Faculty of Psychology. After the completion of the new THINK research building on the former Opel site Mark 51°7, the team will move there https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/think/index.html.en. The research focus of our department is on combining neuroimaging and behavioural measurements with computational models to understand how the human brain learns and uses prior expectations during cognition. More information can be found here: https://blanklab.eu/The position is part of the Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844), an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy, and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework, which conceptualizes episodic memory as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a part of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. When we communicate with others, our perception of their speech is continuously guided by the memory of our past interactions. But how? In this CRC subproject A16 " Integration of episodic traces and semantic other-person models in a social context", we will investigate how memory traces of previously heard dialogues and the other-person model, which contains general semantic knowledge about the person, modify speech perception. This project places the generative model of scenario construction within a social context. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigate how EM traces and other-person models differentially influence the neural representation of speech and language. We are looking for an enthusiastic researcher with a Master's degree in psychology, cognitive science, or a related field and strong programming and statistical skills to carry out the proposed project.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)Start: 01.01.2027, pending funding approvalApply by:  2026-11-30Your tasks:- Organization and execution of experimental research work, from programming experimental setups, data acquisition, and data analysis, to the dissemination of the results- Acquisition of MRI data- Analysis and publication of MRI data- Practice of Open Science Practices- Close collaboration with PIs and ECRs from other subprojectsYour profile:- A Master of Science or an equivalent degree in neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, or a related discipline- Strong programming and statistical skills- Experience in experimental approaches to study predictive processing, memory, learning, and communication- Prior experience with fMRI is an advantage- Experience and keen interest in using large language models- Strong organizational skills- A high level of spoken and written English- Highly self-motivated and eager to learn- Working independently, in a structured manner, and with a focus on results- Enjoy working as part of an interdisciplinary team of researchershttps://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/c0bf34da8b741897fe8de879edc88d7edfbdf8730?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/c0bf34da8b741897fe8de879edc88d7edfbdf8730?ref=AfA)

jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (19.915 hours/week = 50%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for anOutreach Coordinator (m,f,x)The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary research consortium bringing together researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy, and neuroscience. It comprises 18 subprojects led by 22 principal investigators across six universities and is coordinated at Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). CRC 1844 investigates episodic memory—the ability to remember specific events from one’s personal past—from multiple disciplinary perspectives. A central goal of the consortium is to communicate research on episodic memory and its relevance beyond the scientific community, foster dialogue between science and society, and to develop innovative educational and participatory formats for engaging different target groups with research on episodic memory.We are seeking an Outreach Coordinator to lead the strategic development, implementation, and coordination of outreach and science communication activities within CRC 1844. As the central point of contact for outreach, the coordinator will work closely with researchers across the consortium to communicate research on episodic memory to diverse audiences and foster dialogue between science and society. As a member of the coordination team they will develop and implementt public engagement and educational activities, support citizen science initiatives, coordinate the CRC’s digital presence, and collaborate with internal and external partners to strengthen the visibility and societal impact of the consortium’s research.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030, pending funding jobs.description: Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.Unit’s description and purpose: The International Partnerships and Programmes Implementation Unit leads and coordinates system-wide resource mobilisation and partnership development to enable the delivery of Fairtrade’s strategic priorities. It also ensures the effective management of externally funded projects led by Fairtrade International. Our purpose is to secure new financial resources and partnerships that empower Fairtrade and its members to improve the lives of farmers and workers and contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals through quality programmes and projects.  A grant has been secured funded by the European Commission’s LIFE programme for a three year project (June 2025-May 2028) to be implemented in partnership with 5 national Fairtrade organisations in Europe. The aim of the project is to strengthen the capacity of companies, particularly 1000 MSMEs in 12 EU Member States, to comply with the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). The Unit requires the Project Officer to coordinate the project that includes project staff allocated in five national Fairtrade organisations.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:The Project Officer (70% FTE) will play a key role in the project’s coordination, financial and administrative management, and compliance with European Commission requirements. The post holder will take the lead in meeting reporting obligations towards the EC, engaging with stakeholders, and supporting the project's implementation. Specifically, the Project Officer will:- Ensure effective implementation  of the project, organising on-line operational  meetings with partners, documenting agendas and key decisions.- Ensure coordination among all project partners resulting in effective project implementation, including the planning and  delivery of annual in-person project meetings with partners.- Compile a final internal and donor narrative report on project progress and challenges and liaise with donor on requested changes to the project.- Maintain project financial documentation and process financial expenditure (in coordination with the Finance team).- Ensure compliance with and visibility of donor requirements.- Contribute to the implementation of the project’s data management protocols, and monitoring and evaluation plan (in close collaboration with MEL experts).- Act as the primary contact for the European Commission and the Consortium Steering Committee, providing progress updates and reports.- Manage and maintain the project’s risks, assessing their impact, and implementing mitigation strategies in collaboration with project partners and the Consortium Steering Committee to ensure project objectives are met.- Actively engage with other related projects, creating synergies and leveraging complementary efforts.
